Subsequently, the Petitioner approached the Commission for up-gradation of its trading licence from Category ‘IV’ to Category ‘III’ and the Commission vide Order dated 19.2.20216 in Petition No. 212/MP/2015, up-graded the Category ‘IV’ to Category ‘III’ in accordance with the the "Trading Licence Regulations, 2009, subject to the terms and conditions contained in the licence. 6. The matter was called out for the hearing on 25.3.2026. The learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in the instant Petition. Vide Record of Proceedings (“the RoP”) dated 25.3.2026, the Petitioner was directed to submit, on affidavit, within two weeks, a duly signed and audited special balance sheet prepared within 30 days of the filing of the petition, with all pages, including the Auditor’s Report, financial statements, notes, and schedules, duly authenticated by the Auditor. The Petitioner was further directed to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of net worth, current ratio, and liquidity ratio for the grant of a Category I licence in accordance with the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, based on the duly certified, audited special balance sheet. 7. In compliance with the RoP dated 25.3.2026, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 9.4.2026, has submitted the information called for. The Petitioner has submitted that its Balance Sheet is dated 31.1.2026, which is within 30 days immediately preceding the date of filing of the instant Petition, i.e. 2.3.2026. With regard to the Petitioner’s net worth, the Petitioner has submitted that it exceeds the stipulated minimum of Rs. 50 crore or Rs. 75 crore (for between 7000 MUs to 10,000 MUs and beyond 10,000 MUs respectively) is required for a Category I trading licence. In terms of Regulation 9 (2) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, the Commission may consider relaxation of the minimum norms under liquidity ratio and current ratio in view of the significantly higher net worth of the Petitioner. The Petitioner company is financially sound with respect to liquidity for carrying out electricity trade on account of its high net worth [more than 100% of stipulated trade on account of its high net worth]. The Petitioner prayed to exercise the Power to Relax enshrined in Regulation 23 of the Trading 8. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the directions issued vide RoP dated 25.03.2026 have been duly complied with, and requested that the matter be reserved for orders. Considering the submissions made the matter was reserved for the Order. 9. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. Regulation 9(4) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Trading License and other Related Matters) Regulations, 2020 (the Trading Licence Regulations 2020) provides as under: _(c) The Trading Licensee shall be granted an opportunity of being heard by the Commission before taking a decision on the application_ _(1) The Trading Licensee shall comply with the requirements of laws in force and, in particular, the Act, the Rules and the Regulations, Grid Code, orders and directions issued by the Commission from time to time and any of the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions in accordance with law._ 16. Since the Petitioner is not fulfilling the requirement of the current and liquidity ratios, the Commission, vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 25.3.2026, directed the Petitioner to file the status of the current and liquidity ratios. The Petitioner has submitted that its net worth is larger than the stipulated minimum of Rs. 50 crore or Rs. 75 crore required for Category I trading licence and has prayed to relax the minimum norms under liquidity and current ratios in view of the significantly higher net worth of the Petitioner in terms of Regulation 9 (2) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. The Petitioner company is financially sound with respect to liquidity for carrying _“16. Since the Petitioner is not fulfilling the requirement of the liquidity ratio, the Commission, vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 05.06.2025 and RoP dated 10.06.2025, directed the Petitioner to file the status of the liquidity ratio. The Petitioner vide its affidavit dated 16.06.2025 has submitted that the Commission, in its order dated 27.05.2019 in Petition No. 219/TD/2019, granted a Category I Trading Licence to M/s. NTPC Ltd. This decision was made by relaxing the liquidity ratio requirement, as the company demonstrated financial soundness in terms of liquidity for conducting electricity trade and fulfilled all other necessary criteria._ 18. On consideration of the above facts, after an examination, we find that the Petitioner meets the requirements as specified in the Trading Licence Regulations for the grant of a Category 'I' trading licence, Accordingly, we approve the upgradation of the inter-State trading licence of the Applicant from Category ‘III’ to Category ‘I’ with effect from the date of issuance of the order. The licensee shall remain bound by the terms and conditions contained in the various orders issued from time to time and provisions of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. The licensee shall further comply with the provisions of the Payment of Fees Regulations and Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, as amended from time to time. 19. Let an extract copy of this order be sent to the Central Government (Ministry of Power) and the Central Electricity Authority in terms of sub-section (7) of Section 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003, for their information and record. **Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026** CERC Website S.
